text:
The correct increasing order of $\text{C}-\text{H}(\text{A})$, $\text{C}-\text{O}(\text{B})$, $\text{C}=\text{O}(\text{C})$ and $\text{C}\equiv\text{N}(\text{D})$ bonds in terms of covalent bond length is:

(1) $\text{A} < \text{B} < \text{C} < \text{D}$

(2) $\text{A} < \text{D} < \text{C} < \text{B}$

(3) $\text{D} < \text{C} < \text{B} < \text{A}$

(4) $\text{D} < \text{C} < \text{A} < \text{B}$
solution:
$\text{C}-\text{H} \text{ (A)} \quad 107 \text{ pm}$

$\text{C}\equiv\text{N} \text{ (D)} \quad 116 \text{ pm}$

$\text{C}=\text{O} \text{ (C)} \quad 121 \text{ pm}$

$\text{C}-\text{O} \text{ (B)} \quad 143 \text{ pm}

Therefore, increasing order: $\text{A} < \text{D} < \text{C} < \text{B}$.

subject: Chemistry
text:
Given below are two statements :

**Statement I :** The halogen that makes longest bond with hydrogen in $\text{HX}$, has the smallest covalent radius in its group.

**Statement II :** A group 15 element's hydride $\text{EH}_3$ has the lowest boiling point among corresponding hydrides of other group 15 elements. The maximum covalency of that element E is 4.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.

(1) Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
(2) Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
(3) Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
(4) Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

options.1: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
options.2: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
options.3: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
options.4: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

solution:
Bond length order: $\text{HF} < \text{HCl} < \text{HBr} < \text{HI}$. Therefore, HI makes the longest bond with hydrogen, but F has the smallest covalent radius. Thus, Statement I is false.

Boiling point order: $\text{PH}_3 < \text{AsH}_3 < \text{NH}_3 < \text{SbH}_3 < \text{BiH}_3$. $\text{PH}_3$ has the lowest boiling point among group 15 hydrides, and the corresponding element is Phosphorus (P). The maximum possible covalency of phosphorus is 6 (e.g., in $\text{PF}_6^-$), not 4. Thus, Statement II is also false.

subject: Chemistry
text: The energy of first (lowest) Balmer line of $\mathrm{H}$ atom is $\mathrm{x}$ J. The energy (in J) of second Balmer line of $\mathrm{H}$ atom is :
solution:
Transition of first Balmer line:
$n_1 = 2; n_2 = 3$
$\Delta \mathrm{E} = \mathrm{x} = 13.6 (1)^2 \left[ \frac{1}{2^2} - \frac{1}{3^2} \right] \dots \text{(i)}$

Transition of $2^{\text{nd}}$ Balmer line:
$n_1 = 2; n_2 = 4$
$\Delta \mathrm{E} = 13.6 (1)^2 \left[ \frac{1}{2^2} - \frac{1}{4^2} \right] \dots \text{(ii)}$

Divide Eq. (ii) by eq. (i) gives $1.35\mathrm{x}$.

text:

subject: Chemistry
text:
Consider the following aqueous solutions.
I. $2.2\text{ g}$ Glucose in $125\text{ mL}$ of solution.
II. $1.9\text{ g}$ Calcium chloride in $250\text{ mL}$ of solution.
III. $9.0\text{ g}$ Urea in $500\text{ mL}$ of solution.
IV. $20.5\text{ g}$ Aluminium sulphate in $750\text{ mL}$ of solution.
The correct increasing order of boiling point of these solutions will be:
[Given: Molar mass in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$: $\text{H}=1$, $\text{C}=12$, $\text{N}=14$, $\text{O}=16$, $\text{Cl}=35.5$, $\text{Ca}=40$, $\text{Al}=27$ and $\text{S}=32$]
solution:
$\Delta T_b = i \cdot K_b \cdot m$
For dilute solution ($M \approx m$)
(I) $\text{M}_{\text{glucose}} = \frac{2.2}{180} \times \frac{1000}{125} = 0.098$, $i \times m = 0.098 \times 1$
(II) $\text{M}_{\text{CaCl}_2} = \frac{1.9}{111} \times \frac{1000}{250} = 0.068$, $i \times m = 0.068 \times 3$
(III) $\text{M}_{\text{urea}} = \frac{9}{60} \times \frac{1000}{500} = 0.3$, $i \times m = 0.3 \times 1$
(IV) $\text{M}_{\text{Al}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3} = \frac{20.5}{342} \times \frac{1000}{750} \simeq 0.08$, $i \times m = 0.08 \times 5$
Order of $\Delta T_b = \text{Al}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3 > \text{Urea} > \text{CaCl}_2 > \text{Glucose}$
So order of $\text{BP} = \text{Al}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3 > \text{Urea} > \text{CaCl}_2 > \text{Glucose}$
So Answer will be $\text{I} < \text{II} < \text{III} < \text{IV}$

text:
Given below are two statements :
**Statement (I) :** Benzyl chloride reacts faster in $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ mechanism than ethyl chloride.
**Statement (II) :** Ethyl carbocation intermediate is less stabilized by hyperconjugation than benzyl carbocation by resonance.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.1: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.2: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
options.3: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options.4: Statement I is false but Statement II is true

solution:
Rate of $\text{S}_\text{N}1 \propto \text{Stability of carbocation}$
Order of stability of carbocation :
$\text{Ph}-\overset{\oplus}{\text{C}}\text{H}_2 > \text{CH}_3-\overset{\oplus}{\text{C}}\text{H}_2$
Hyperconjugation in $\text{CH}_3-\overset{\oplus}{\text{C}}\text{H}_2$
Resonance in $\text{Ph}-\overset{\oplus}{\text{C}}\text{H}_2$
Thus, both statements are true.

text:
"P" is hydrocarbon of molecular formula $\text{C}_8\text{H}_{14}$. On ozonolysis, "P" forms "Q". "Q" on treatment with alkali under reflux condition produces "R", which on treatment with $\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$ gives a yellow precipitate. Acidification of the solution gives "S". The structure of "S" given below :
\begin{center}\begin{tabular}{c}\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8]\draw (0,0) -- (1,0) -- (1.5,0.8) -- (0.8,1.5) -- (0,1) -- cycle;\draw (0.8,1.5) -- (1.3,1.5) node[right] {$\text{CH}_3$};\draw (0.8,0) -- (0.8,-0.8) node[below] {$\text{COOH}$};\end{tikzpicture}\end{tabular}\end{center}
The correct structure of "P" is
solution:
1. Ozonolysis of 1,2-dimethylcyclohexene gives a dicarbonyl compound (Q) which contains a keto and an aldehyde or two keto groups depending on the cleavage. Specifically, 1,2-dimethylcyclohexene gives hexane-2,5-dione derivative upon reductive ozonolysis.
2. Intramolecular aldol condensation of Q with alkali under reflux produces R.
3. Treatment of R with $\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$ (haloform reaction) gives a yellow precipitate of iodoform ($\text{CHI}_3$) and acid salt, which upon acidification yields S.
4. Tracing backwards, the structure of P is 1,2-dimethylcyclohexene.

subject: Chemistry
text:
Given below are two statements:

**Statement I :** Sucrose is dextrorotatory. However sucrose upon hydrolysis gives a solution having mixture of products. This solution shows laevorotation.

**Statement II :** Hydrolysis of sucrose gives glucose and fructose. Since the laevorotation of glucose is more than the dextrorotation of fructose the resulting solution becomes laevorotatory.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.

(1) Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
(2) Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
(3) Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
(4) Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

options.1: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
options.2: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
options.3: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
options.4: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

solution:
Reaction: $\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{22}\text{O}_{11} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{HCl}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6 \text{ (D-Glucose)} + \text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6 \text{ (D-Fructose)}$
$[\alpha]_{\text{D-sucrose}} = +66.5^\circ$, $[\alpha]_{\text{D-Glucose}} = +52.5^\circ$, $[\alpha]_{\text{D-Fructose}} = -92.4^\circ$

Sucrose is dextrorotatory and the hydrolysed product is laevorotatory because the laevorotation of fructose ($-92.4^\circ$) is greater in magnitude than the dextrorotation of glucose ($+52.5^\circ$). Thus, Statement I is true, but Statement II is false because it incorrectly states that the laevorotation of *glucose* is more than the dextrorotation of *fructose*.

subject: Chemistry
text: A hydroxy compound (X) with molar mass $122 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$ is acetylated with acetic anhydride, using a large excess of the reagent ensuring complete acetylation of all hydroxyl groups. The product obtained has a molar mass of $290 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$. The number of hydroxyl groups present in compound (X) is :
solution:
Let the number of $-\text{OH}$ groups be $n$. Each acetylation replaces an $-\text{H}$ of an $-\text{OH}$ group with an acetyl group ($-\text{COCH}_3$, mass increase of $43 - 1 = 42 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$ per group).
$\text{Molar mass of product} = \text{Molar mass of } (X) + n \times (42)$
$290 = 122 + n \times 42$
$n \times 42 = 290 - 122 = 168$
$n = \frac{168}{42} = 4$

subject: Chemistry
text:
$$\text{Ph}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 \xrightarrow[(\text{PhCOO})_2]{\text{HBr}} \text{Product}$$
Consider the above reaction:
A. The reaction proceeds through a more stable radical intermediate.
B. The role of peroxide is to generate $\dot{\text{H}}$ (Hydrogen radical).
C. During this reaction, benzene is formed as a biproduct.
D. 1-Bromo-2-phenylethane is formed as the minor product.
E. The same reaction in absence of peroxide proceeds via carbocation intermediate.
Identify the correct statements. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
solution:
A. Free radical addition of HBr in the presence of peroxide proceeds via the formation of a more stable free radical intermediate.
B. Peroxide generates $\text{Br}^{\bullet}$ radical, not $\dot{\text{H}}$.
C. Benzene is formed as a byproduct during the decomposition of benzoyl peroxide.
D. 1-Bromo-2-phenylethane is the major anti-Markovnikov product, while 1-bromo-1-phenylethane is the minor product.
E. In the absence of peroxide, addition of HBr follows Markovnikov's rule and proceeds via a carbocation intermediate.
Thus, statements A, C, and E are correct.

text:
For the following Friedel Craft's alkylation reaction, which of the statements are correct ?
$$\text{Benzene} + \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl} \xrightarrow[\text{Anhydrous}]{\text{AlCl}_3} \text{Alkylbenzene}$$
A. Major product is n-propyl benzene.
B. iso-propyl carbocation intermediate is also generated.
C. Multiple substitution is inevitable.
D. Introducing electron-donating substituent on benzene will not produce any alkylbenzene.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution:
1. The reaction proceeds via the formation of the primary propyl carbocation which undergoes rearrangement to form the more stable iso-propyl carbocation: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2^+ \rightarrow \text{CH}_3-\overset{+}{\text{CH}}-\text{CH}_3$. Thus, Statement B is correct.
2. Alkyl groups are activating groups, making the ring more reactive towards further alkylation, hence multiple substitution is inevitable. Statement C is correct.
3. Statement A is incorrect because the major product is iso-propylbenzene (cumene), not n-propylbenzene.
4. Statement D is incorrect because activating groups facilitate electrophilic aromatic substitution.
Therefore, B and C are correct.

text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement-I : Methane can be prepared by decarboxylation of sodium ethanoate, Kolbe's electrolysis of sodium acetate and reaction of $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$ with water.
Statement-II : Methane cannot be prepared from unsaturated hydrocarbons and by Wurtz reaction.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.

options.1: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true.
options.2: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false.
options.3: Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false.
options.4: Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true.

solution:
Methane cannot be prepared by Kolbe's electrolysis process. So, statement-1 is false.
$$2\text{CH}_3-\text{C}-\text{ONa} \xrightarrow{\text{Kolbe electrolysis}} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_3 + 2\text{CO}_2 + 2\text{NaOH} + \text{H}_2$$
Methane also cannot be prepared by Wurtz reaction, so statement-2 is true.
$$2\text{R}-\text{X} \xrightarrow[\text{Wurtz reaction}]{\text{Na, dry ether}} \text{R}-\text{R} + 2\text{NaX}$$
If $\text{R} = -\text{CH}_3$, then ethane is formed, not methane.

Compound [D] is a methyl ketone which gives a positive haloform test.

text: At $27^{\circ}\text{C}$ in presence of a catalyst, activation energy of a reaction is lowered by $10\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. The logarithm ratio of $\frac{\text{k (catalysed)}}{\text{k (uncatalysed)}}$ is .... (Consider that the frequency factor for both the reactions is same)
solution:
$$\frac{\text{K}_{\text{catalyst}}}{\text{K}_{\text{uncatalyst}}} = e^{\frac{\Delta\text{E}_{\text{a}}}{\text{RT}}}$$
$$\ln \frac{\text{K}_{\text{catalyst}}}{\text{K}_{\text{uncatalyst}}} = \frac{\Delta\text{E}_{\text{a}}}{\text{RT}}$$
$$\log \frac{\text{K}_{\text{catalyst}}}{\text{K}_{\text{uncatalyst}}} = \frac{\Delta\text{E}_{\text{a}}}{2.303\text{RT}}$$
$$= \frac{10 \times 1000}{2.303 \times 8.314 \times 300}$$
$$\log \frac{\text{K}_{\text{catalyst}}}{\text{K}_{\text{uncatalyst}}} = 1.741$$

**Statement-I** : The condensation reaction between $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{O}$ and $\text{H}_2\text{N}-\text{N}-\text{C}-\text{NH}_2$ under optimum pH will produce $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{N}-\text{C}-\text{NH}_2$

options.2: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false.
options.3: Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false.

The $-\text{NH}_2$ group away from the carbonyl group is more nucleophilic and attacks the carbonyl carbon during condensation. Hence, Statement-I is incorrect.

subject: Chemistry
text:
Given below are two statements :

**Statement-I** : Due to increase in van der Waals forces, the order of boiling points is $CH_3CH_2CH_2I > CH_3CH_2I > CH_3I$.

**Statement-II** : As $p$-dichlorobenzene is more symmetric, its melting point is higher than $o$-dichlorobenzene, however its boiling point is lower than $o$-dichlorobenzene.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.1: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true.
options.2: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false.
options.3: Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false.
options.4: Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true.

solution:
Statement-I: As the molecular size and surface area increase, van der Waals forces increase, leading to higher boiling points. Thus, the order $CH_3CH_2CH_2I > CH_3CH_2I > CH_3I$ is correct.

Statement-II: $p$-dichlorobenzene is more symmetric and fits better in the crystal lattice, giving it a higher melting point than the ortho isomer. However, due to its symmetry and zero dipole moment, its intermolecular forces are slightly weaker in the liquid state compared to the polar ortho isomer, resulting in a lower boiling point. 

Therefore, both statements are true.

solution:

$$\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 + \text{KI} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} \text{I}_2 + \text{Cr}^{3+}$$

text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : '$\text{C}-\text{Cl}$' bond is stronger in $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{Cl}$ than $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl}$
Statement II : The given optically active molecule,
$$\text{Me}\underbrace{\text{Ph}}_{\text{Et}}\text{C}-\text{Cl}$$
on hydrolysis gives a solution that can rotate the plane polarized light.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below

options.1: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
options.2: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.3: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
options.4: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

solution:
Statement-I :
$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\ddot{\text{Cl}}:\longleftrightarrow \stackrel{\ominus}{\text{CH}}_2-\text{CH}=\stackrel{\oplus}{\text{Cl}}:\longleftrightarrow \stackrel{\ominus\delta}{\text{CH}}_2-\text{CH}=\stackrel{\oplus\delta}{\text{Cl}}$$
$\text{C}-\text{Cl}$ bond is strong in vinyl chloride because of double bond character.
Statement-II :
Hydrolysis via $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ gives a racemic mixture.
Racemic mixture is optically inactive, which can not rotate PPL.

text: The heat of atomisation of methane and ethane are '$x$ kJ mol$^{-1}$' and '$y$ kJ mol$^{-1}$' respectively. The longest wavelength ($\lambda$) of light capable of breaking the C-C bond can be expressed in SI unit as :
solution:
$\text{CH}_4(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{C}(\text{g}) + 4\text{H}(\text{g}); \quad \Delta_r \text{H} = x \text{ kJ/mole}$
$\text{C}_2\text{H}_6(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\text{C}(\text{g}) + 6\text{H}(\text{g}); \quad \Delta_r \text{H} = y \text{ kJ/mole}$
$1000x = 4 \times \varepsilon_{\text{C-H}}$
$1000y = 1 \times \varepsilon_{\text{C-C}} + 6 \times \varepsilon_{\text{C-H}}$
$\varepsilon_{\text{C-C}} = \left[y - \frac{3x}{2}\right] \times 1000 = \frac{hc}{\lambda} \cdot N_A$
$('\lambda')$ wavelength of photon $= \frac{hc N_A}{[4y - 6x] \times 250}$

text:

(C) (Y) and (Z) react with \text{HCN} with same rates

text: The strongest conjugate acid will result from

text:
Consider compounds A, B and C with following structural formulae:
$\text{A} = \text{CH}_3 - \text{CH}_2 - \text{CH}_2 - \text{CH}_2 - \text{CH}_2 - \text{OH}$
$\text{B} = \text{CH}_2 = \text{CH} - \text{CH}_2 - \text{CH}_2 - \text{CH}_3$
$\text{C} = \text{HO} - \text{CH}_2 - \text{CH}_2 - \text{CH}(\text{OH}) - \text{CH}_3$
For the conversion of B from A, reagent (D) required is $\underline{\quad\quad\quad}$ and structural formula of product (E) obtained when C undergoes same reaction using excess reagent (D) is $\underline{\quad\quad\quad}$
solution: For conversion of alcohol A ($\\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{OH}$) to alkene B ($\\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$), dehydration of alcohol is required using concentrated $\\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ or $\\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$. When diol C ($\\text{HO}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{OH})-\text{CH}_3$) reacts with excess of the same dehydrating reagent, it undergoes double dehydration to yield a conjugated diene, 1,3-butadiene ($\\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$). Thus, option (4) is correct.

subject: Chemistry
text:
Given below are two statements :

**Statement-I** : Heating benzamide with bromine in an ethanolic solution of sodium hydroxide will give benzylamine.

**Statement-II** : Nitration of aniline with $\text{HNO}_3/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ at $288\text{ K}$ produces $m$-nitroaniline in higher amount than $o$-nitroaniline (pH adjusted).

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.1: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true.
options.2: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false.
options.3: Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false.
options.4: Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true.

solution:
**Statement-I:** Heating benzamide with bromine and $\text{NaOH}$ undergoes Hoffmann bromamide degradation reaction to give aniline ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$), not benzylamine. Hence, Statement-I is false.

**Statement-II:** Nitration of aniline gives a significant amount of m-nitroaniline due to protonation of aniline in strong acidic medium forming the meta-directing anilinium ion. Hence, Statement-II is true.

text:

Acidification with $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$ gives the final product (P) corresponding to option (3).

subject: Chemistry
text: At $298\text{ K}$, the mole percentage of $\text{N}_2(\text{g})$ in air is $80\%$. Water is in equilibrium with air at a pressure of $10\text{ atm}$. What is the mole fraction of $\text{N}_2(\text{g})$ in water at $298\text{ K}$ ? ($\text{K}_H$ for $\text{N}_2$ is $6.5 \times 10^7\text{ mm Hg}$)
solution:
$P_{\text{N}_2} = \text{K}_H \cdot \text{X}_{\text{N}_2}$
$P_{\text{N}_2} = 0.8 \times 10 = 8\text{ atm}$
$8 \times 760 = 6.5 \times 10^7 \times \text{X}_{\text{N}_2}$
$\text{X}_{\text{N}_2} = \frac{8 \times 760}{6.5 \times 10^7}$
$\text{X}_{\text{N}_2} = 9.35 \times 10^{-5}$.

The correct order regarding the reactivity of these compounds with $	ext{Ph}-	ext{N}\equiv	ext{N}^+ 	ext{Cl}^-$ under optimum but slightly acidic medium is :

subject: Chemistry
text:
Identify the incorrect statements:

$\text{A. } \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$ is a stronger base than $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$.

$\text{B. } \text{p-}\text{CH}_3\text{O}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{NH}_2$ can be synthesized by Gabriel phthalimide synthesis.

$\text{C. } \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{CONH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2, \text{NaOH}} \text{Primary aromatic amine}$

$\text{D. } \text{p-NO}_2\text{C}_6\text{H}_4\text{NH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{(i) } \text{NaNO}_2, \text{HCl}, 0^\circ\text{C}} \text{ product } \xrightarrow{\text{(ii) } \Delta} \text{ will dissolve in } \text{NaOH}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
solution:
Statement A is correct because benzylamine is a stronger base than aniline (due to absence of resonance stabilization of the lone pair with the benzene ring in benzylamine).
Statement B is incorrect because aromatic primary amines cannot be prepared by Gabriel phthalimide synthesis as aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with potassium phthalimide under mild conditions.
Statement C is incorrect because $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{CONH}_2$ on Hofmann bromamide degradation gives $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$, which is a primary aliphatic amine (benzylamine), not a primary aromatic amine.
Statement D is correct.
Thus, the incorrect statements are B and C.

text:
The number of compounds from the following which can undergo reaction with $\text{Br}_2/\text{KOH}$ (alcoholic) to give respective products and these respective products can also be obtained separately by Gabriel phthalimide reaction is:
- $\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{NH}_2$
- $\text{H}_5\text{C}_6-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{NH}_2$
- $\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{NH}_2$
- $\text{H}_{11}\text{C}_6-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{NHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$
- $(\text{H}_3\text{C})_3\text{C}-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{NHCH}_3$
- $\text{H}_{11}\text{C}_6-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{NH}_2$
solution:
Gabriel phthalimide reaction yields primary aliphatic amines. The $\text{Br}_2/\text{KOH}$ reaction converts primary amides into primary amines with one carbon less.
Primary amines that can be prepared by both methods are those derived from simple primary amides (excluding secondary amides and aromatic amides where Gabriel synthesis or Hoffmann degradation may have limitations depending on exact aryl constraints, typically resulting in 3 valid candidates).

subject: Chemistry
text:
Which statements are True?
A. In Hoffmann bromamide degradation, 4 moles of $	ext{NaOH}$ and 2 moles of $	ext{Br}_2$ are consumed per mole of an amide.
B. Hoffmann bromamide reaction is not given by alkyl amides.
C. Primary amines can be synthesized by Hoffmann bromamide degradation.
D. Secondary amide on reaction with $	ext{Br}_2$ and $	ext{NaOH}$ will give secondary amine.
E. The by-products of Hoffmann degradation are $	ext{Na}_2	ext{CO}_3$, $	ext{NaBr}$ and $	ext{H}_2	ext{O}$.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution:
The stoichiometric equation for Hoffmann bromamide degradation is:
$$	ext{R}-	ext{CONH}_2 + 4	ext{NaOH} + 	ext{Br}_2 ightarrow 	ext{R}-	ext{NH}_2 + 	ext{Na}_2	ext{CO}_3 + 2	ext{NaBr} + 2	ext{H}_2	ext{O}$$
- Statement (A) is False because 1 mole of $	ext{Br}_2$ is consumed (not 2 moles).
- Statement (B) is False because alkyl amides do undergo this reaction.
- Statement (C) is True (primary amines are synthesized).
- Statement (D) is False (secondary amides do not give this reaction).
- Statement (E) is True (by-products are $	ext{Na}_2	ext{CO}_3$, $	ext{NaBr}$, and $	ext{H}_2	ext{O}$).
Thus, statements C and E are true.

text:
For the reaction, $\mathrm{N}_2\mathrm{O}_4 \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NO}_2$, graph is plotted as shown below. Identify correct statements.
A. Standard free energy change for the reaction is $-5.40 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.
B. As $\Delta G^{\ominus}$ in graph is positive, $\mathrm{N}_2\mathrm{O}_4$ will not dissociate into $\mathrm{NO}_2$ at all.
C. Reverse reaction will go to completion.
D. When $1$ mole of $\mathrm{N}_2\mathrm{O}_4$ changes into equilibrium mixture, value of $\Delta G^{\ominus} = -0.84 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
E. When $2$ mole of $\mathrm{NO}_2$ changes into equilibrium mixture, $\Delta G^{\ominus}$ for equilibrium mixture is $-6.24 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution:
(A) $\Delta_r G^{\circ} = G_{\text{B}}^{\circ} - G_{\text{A}}^{\circ} = +\text{ve}$
(B) $\Delta_r G^{\circ} = +\text{ve}$, $\mathrm{N}_2\mathrm{O}_4$ will partially dissociate into $\mathrm{NO}_2$.
(C) For reverse reaction, it is partially completed as there is equilibrium at E.
(D) For $1$ mole $\mathrm{N}_2\mathrm{O}_4$; $\Delta_r \mathrm{G}^{\circ} = -0.84 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
(E) For $2$ mole $\mathrm{NO}_2$; $\Delta \mathrm{G}^{\circ} = -5.4 - 0.84 = -6.24 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : The correct order in terms of bond dissociation enthalpy is $\text{Cl}_2 > \text{Br}_2 > \text{F}_2 > \text{I}_2$

Statement II : The correct trend in the covalent character of the metal halides is $[\text{SnCl}_4 > \text{SnCl}_2]$, $[\text{PbCl}_4 > \text{PbCl}_2]$ and $[\text{UF}_4 > \text{UF}_6]$

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.1: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options.2: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.3: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
options.4: Both Statement I and Statement II are false

solution:
Statement-I :
Bond energy order is $\text{Cl}_2 > \text{Br}_2 > \text{F}_2 > \text{I}_2$
Bond energy increases with increase in bond order.

Statement-II :
Correct order of covalent character
According to the Fajan's rule, higher the charge on cation, greater is the covalent character.
$\text{PbCl}_2 < \text{PbCl}_4$,
$\text{UF}_6 > \text{UF}_4$ (Incorrectly given as $\text{UF}_4 > \text{UF}_6$ in statement II),
$\text{SnCl}_4 > \text{SnCl}_2$
Thus, Statement II is false.

subject: Chemistry
text:
The correct statements from the following are :
(A) Ionic radii of trivalent cations of group 13 elements decreases down the group.
(B) Electronegativity of group 13 elements decreases down the group.
(C) Among the group 13 elements, Boron has highest first ionisation enthalpy.
(D) The trichloride and triiodide of group 13 elements are covalent in nature.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution:
(A) Ionic radii increases down the group ($B^{+3} < Al^{+3} < Ga^{+3} < In^{+3} < Tl^{+3}$). Thus, statement A is incorrect.
(B) Electronegativity decreases initially then increases ($B > Tl > In > Ga > Al$). Thus, statement B is incorrect.
(C) Boron has the highest first ionization enthalpy among group 13 elements ($B > Tl > Ga > Al > In$). Thus, statement C is correct.
(D) Trichlorides and triiodides of group 13 elements are covalent in nature due to high polarising power. Thus, statement D is correct.

Statement I : 1,2-diaminobenzene can be synthesized from 1,2-dibutylbenzene (or similar alkyl derivative shown in structure) using simpler reagents in the order i) Acidic $	ext{KMnO}_4$, ii) Ammonia, iii) Bromine and alkali

Statement II : 4-methylaniline can be converted into 2,6-dibromo-1-methylbenzene using reagents in the order (i) $	ext{Bromine-H}_2	ext{O}$ (ii) $	ext{NaNO}_2/	ext{HCl} 	ext{ (0-5 }^\circ	ext{C)}$ (iii) aq. $	ext{H}_3	ext{PO}_2$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below

options.1: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
options.2: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options.3: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.4: Statement I is false but Statement II is true

solution: Statement-I involves oxidation of alkyl side chains using acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$ to dicarboxylic acids, conversion to diamides with ammonia, followed by Hofmann bromamide degradation to yield 1,2-diaminobenzene. This sequence is correct.\nStatement-II involves bromination of 4-methylaniline to direct bromines ortho to the amino group, followed by diazotization and reduction ($\text{deamination}$) using $\text{aq. H}_3\text{PO}_2$ to remove the $-\text{NH}_2$ group, successfully yielding 2,6-dibromotoluene. This sequence is also correct.\nTherefore, both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are true.

text:
Arrange the following carbanions in the decreasing order of stability
I. $p-\text{Br}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\stackrel{\ominus}{\text{CH}}_2$
II. $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\stackrel{\ominus}{\text{CH}}_2$
III. $p-\text{CH}_3\text{O}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\stackrel{\ominus}{\text{CH}}_2$
IV. $p-\text{CHO}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\stackrel{\ominus}{\text{CH}}_2$
V. $p-\text{CH}_3-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\stackrel{\ominus}{\text{CH}}_2$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution: Electron withdrawing groups increase the stability of carbanions and electron donating groups decrease the stability of carbanions. -CHO is a strong -M group (IV), Br exhibits -I and +M effects (I), H has no substituent effect (II), $-\text{CH}_3$ is +I/+H (V), and $-\text{OCH}_3$ is a strong +M group (III). Thus, the decreasing order of stability is $\text{IV} > \text{I} > \text{II} > \text{V} > \text{III}$.

text: Consider the following reactions. AlCl}_3} (X)\text{Major product}$

text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: When an electric discharge is passed through gaseous hydrogen, the hydrogen molecules dissociate and the energetically excited hydrogen atoms produce electromagnetic radiation of discrete frequencies.
Statement II: The frequency of second line of Balmer series obtained from $	ext{He}^+$ is equal to that of first line of Lyman series obtained from hydrogen atom.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.1: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.2: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
options.3: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
options.4: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

solution:
For 1st line of lyman series in H-atom:
$$ rac{1}{\lambda} = R(1)^2\left( rac{1}{1^2} -  rac{1}{2^2}ight) =  rac{3R}{4}$$
For 2nd line of Balmer series of $	ext{He}^+$:
$$ rac{1}{\lambda'} = R(2)^2\left( rac{1}{2^2} -  rac{1}{4^2}ight) = 4R 	imes  rac{3}{16} =  rac{3R}{4}$$
As $\lambda$ and $\lambda'$ are equal, the frequency of these lines will also be equal. Hence both statements are true.

subject: Chemistry
text:
Consider the general reaction given below at $400\text{ K}$
$$x\text{A(g)} \rightleftharpoons y\text{B(g)}$$
The values of $\text{K}_p$ and $\text{K}_c$ are studied under the same condition of temperature but variation in x and y.
(i) $\text{K}_p = 85.87$ and $\text{K}_c = 2.586$ appropriate units
(ii) $\text{K}_p = 0.862$ and $\text{K}_c = 28.62$ appropriate units
The value of x and y in (i) and (ii) respectively are:
solution:
For reaction (i) : $\text{K}_p > \text{K}_c \implies \Delta n_g > 0 \implies y - x > 0$.
$85.87 = 2.586(0.0821 \times 400)^{y-x}$
Solving $y - x = 1$.
For reaction (ii) : $\text{K}_p < \text{K}_c \implies \Delta n_g < 0 \implies y - x < 0$.

subject: Chemistry
text: A student has been given a compound "x" of molecular formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_7\text{N}$. 'x' is sparingly soluble in water. However, on addition of dilute mineral acid, 'x' becomes soluble in water. 'x' when treated with $\text{CHCl}_3$ and $\text{KOH (alc.)}$ 'y' is produced. 'y' has a specific unpleasant smell. On treatment with benzenesulphonyl chloride, 'x' gives a compound 'z' which is soluble in alkali. The number of different "H" atoms present in 'z' is:-
solution:
1. Compound 'x' is $	ext{C}_6	ext{H}_7	ext{N}$, which is aniline ($	ext{C}_6	ext{H}_5	ext{NH}_2$). It is a primary amine, hence it gives carbosylamine test with $	ext{CHCl}_3$ and alcoholic $	ext{KOH}$ to form phenyl isocyanide (isoquinoline/carbylamine derivative, 'y') which has an unpleasant smell.
2. Aniline reacts with benzenesulphonyl chloride (Hinsberg's reagent) to form $N$-phenylbenzenesulphonamide ('z'). Since it is a secondary amide derivative containing an acidic hydrogen attached to nitrogen, compound 'z' is soluble in alkali.
3. Formula of 'z' is $	ext{C}_6	ext{H}_5-	ext{NH}-	ext{SO}_2-	ext{C}_6	ext{H}_5$. Counting the different types of hydrogen atoms:
- 5 hydrogens on the monosubstituted benzene ring attached to $-	ext{SO}_2-$
- 1 hydrogen attached to nitrogen ($-	ext{NH}-)$
- 1 hydrogen on the phenyl ring attached to $-	ext{NH}-$ (though symmetry/positions matter, counting unique chemical environments for H atoms).
Total number of different H atoms present in 'z' is 7.

subject: Chemistry
text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : $\text{K} > \text{Mg} > \text{Al} > \text{B}$ is the correct order in terms of metallic character.
Statement II : Atomic radius is always greater than the ionic radius for any element.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below

options.1: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.2: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
options.3: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
options.4: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

solution: Metallic character increases down the group and decreases along a period. Thus K (Group 1) > Mg (Group 2) > Al (Group 13) > B (Group 13) is true for metallic character. Hence Statement I is true. For Statement II, while cationic radius is indeed smaller than atomic radius, anionic radius is always larger than atomic radius. Thus, Statement II is false.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

subject: Chemistry
text: Pre-exponential factors of two different reactions of same order are identical. Let activation energy of first reaction exceeds the activation energy of second reaction by $20\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. If $k_1$ and $k_2$ are the rate constants of first and second reaction respectively at $300\text{ K}$, then $\ln \frac{k_2}{k_1}$ will be ........ . (nearest integer) [$R = 8.3\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$]
solution:
According to Arrhenius equation:
$\ln k_1 = \ln A -  rac{E_1}{300R}$
$\ln k_2 = \ln A -  rac{E_2}{300R}$
$\ln\left( rac{k_2}{k_1}ight) =  rac{E_1 - E_2}{300R} =  rac{20 	imes 1000}{300 	imes R} =  rac{20000}{300 	imes 8.33} \approx 8.032$
Rounding to the nearest integer gives 8.

subject: Chemistry
text: The first and second ionization constants of $\text{H}_2\text{X}$ are $2.5 \times 10^{-8}$ and $1.0 \times 10^{-13}$ respectively. The concentration of $\text{X}^{2-}$ in $0.1\text{ M}\text{ H}_2\text{X}$ solution is ______ $\times 10^{-15}\text{ M}$. (Nearest Integer)
solution:
$\text{H}_2\text{X} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+ + \text{HX}^-$
Initial/Equilibrium:
$0.1-x \quad x+y \quad x-y$

$2.5 \times 10^{-8} = \frac{(x+y)(x-y)}{0.1-x}$

$\text{HX}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+ + \text{X}^{2-}$
$x-y \quad x+y \quad y$

$1 \times 10^{-13} = \frac{(x+y)(y)}{x-y}$

Approximate : $\text{K}_{a_1} \gg \text{K}_{a_2} \Rightarrow \text{So } x \gg y$.
$x+y \approx x, \; x-y \approx x$

$10^{-13} = \frac{x \cdot y}{x}$
$y = 10^{-13}$
$[\text{X}^{2-}] = 10^{-13}$
$[\text{X}^{2-}] = 100 \times 10^{-15}$

text:
Consider the following electrochemical cell : $\text{Pt} \mid \text{O}_2(\text{g}) (1 \text{bar}) \mid \text{HCl} (\text{aq}) \parallel \text{M}^{2+}(\text{aq}, 1.0 \text{ M}) \mid \text{M}(\text{s})$
The $\text{pH}$ above which, oxygen gas would start to evolve at anode is _______ (nearest integer).
Given : $\left[\begin{array}{c} E_{\text{M}^{2+}/\text{M}}^0 = 0.994 \text{ V} \\ E_{\text{O}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O}}^0 = 1.23 \text{ V} \end{array}\right]$ standard reduction potential and $\frac{RT}{F}(2.303) = 0.059 \text{ V}$ at the given condition

$E = E^0 - \frac{0.059}{2} \log \left[ \frac{[\text{H}^+]^2 \times P_{\text{O}_2}^{1/2}}{1} \right]$

subject: Chemistry
text:
$ ext{X}_2( ext{g}) + ext{Y}_2( ext{g}) ightleftharpoons 2 ext{Z}( ext{g})$

$ ext{X}_2( ext{g})$ and $ ext{Y}_2( ext{g})$ are added to a $1\text{ L}$ flask and it is found that the system attains the above equilibrium at $\text{T(K)}$ with the number of moles of $\text{X}_2(\text{g})$, $\text{Y}_2(\text{g})$ and $\text{Z}(\text{g})$ being $3$, $3$ and $9\text{ mol}$ respectively (equilibrium moles). Under this conditions of equilibrium, $10\text{ mol}$ of $\text{Z}(\text{g})$ is added to the flask and the temperature is maintained at $\text{T(K)}$. Then the number of moles of $\text{Z}(\text{g})$ in the flask when the new equilibrium is established is ________. (Nearest integer)
solution:
$$\text{X}_2(\text{g}) + \text{Y}_2(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{Z}(\text{g})$$
$$K_c = \frac{(9)^2}{3 \times 3} = 9$$
Now $10$ moles of $\text{Z}$ are added then reaction will move in backward direction.

$$\begin{array}{lccc} & \text{X}_2(\text{g}) & + \text{Y}_2(\text{g}) & \rightleftharpoons 2\text{Z}(\text{g}) \\ \text{Initial} & 3 & 3 & 19 \\ \text{At Eq.} & 3+X & 3+X & 19-2X \end{array}$$

$$K_c = \frac{(19-2X)^2}{(3+X)(3+X)} = 9$$
$$\frac{19-2X}{3+X} = 3$$
$$19 - 2X = 9 + 3X$$
$$10 = 5X$$
$$X = 2$$
At equilibrium $\implies$ moles of $\text{Z} = 19 - 2 \times 2 = 15\text{ moles}$

subject: Chemistry
text:
Electricity is passed through an acidic solution of $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ till all the $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ was exhausted, leading to the deposition of $300\text{ mg}$ of $\text{Cu}$ metal. However, a current of $600\text{ mA}$ was continued to pass through the same solution for another $28\text{ minutes}$ by keeping the total volume of the solution fixed at $200\text{ mL}$. The total volume of oxygen evolved at STP during the entire process is ______ $\text{mL}$. (Nearest integer)
[Given :
$\text{Cu}^{2+}(\text{aq}) + 2\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{Cu}(\text{s}) \quad E_{\text{red}}^0 = +0.34\text{V}$
$\text{O}_2(\text{g}) + 4\text{H}^+ + 4\text{e}^- \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \quad E_{\text{red}}^0 = +1.23\text{V}$
Molar mass of $\text{Cu} = 63.54\text{ g mol}^{-1}$
Molar mass of $\text{O}_2 = 32\text{ g mol}^{-1}$
Faraday Constant = $96500\text{ C mol}^{-1}$
Molar volume at STP = $22.4\text{ L}$ ]
solution:
$\text{Eq of Cu} = \text{Eq of O}_2$
$$\frac{300 \times 10^{-3} \times 2}{63.54} = n_{\text{O}_2} \times 4$$
$$2.36 \times 10^{-3} = n_{\text{O}_2} \text{ (from deposition)}$$
When current is further passed:
$$n_{\text{O}_2} \times 4 = \frac{600 \times 28 \times 60}{96500 \times 1000}$$
$$n_{\text{O}_2} = 2.611 \times 10^{-3}$$
Total $\text{O}_2$ released:
$$= [10^{-3} \times (2.36 + 2.611)] \times 22400\text{ ml}$$
$$= 111.35\text{ ml}$$

subject: Chemistry
text:
If $3.365\text{ g}$ of ethanol ($l$) burnt completely in a bomb calorimeter at $298.15\text{ K}$, the heat produced is $99.472\text{ kJ}$. The $[\Delta\mathrm{H}_\mathrm{f}^\circ]$ of ethanol at $298.15\text{ K}$ is __________ $\times 10^2\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. (Nearest integer)

Given :
Standard enthalpy of combustion of graphite $= -393.5\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
Standard enthalpy of formation of water ($l$) $= -285.8\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
Molar mass in $\text{gmol}^{-1}$ of $\mathrm{C}$, $\mathrm{H}$, $\mathrm{O}$ are $12$, $1$ and $16$ respectively.
solution:
$\Delta\mathrm{U}_{\text{combustion}}^\circ = \frac{-q}{\text{moles}} = \frac{-99.472}{3.365/46} \Rightarrow 1359.8\text{ KJ/mole}$

$\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{OH}(\ell) + 3\mathrm{O}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}_2(\text{g}) + 3\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\ell)$; $\Delta\mathrm{H}_\mathrm{r}^\circ = \Delta\mathrm{H}_\mathrm{C}^\circ$

$\Delta\mathrm{H}_\mathrm{C}^\circ = \Delta\mathrm{U}^\circ + \Delta_n\mathrm{RT}$
$= -1359.8 + \frac{(-1) \times 8.314 \times 298.15}{1000}$
$= -1362.7\text{ KJ/mole}$

$-1362.27 = [2 \times (-393.5) + 3 \times (-285.8)] - \Delta\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{f}\, \mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{OH}(\ell)}^\circ$
$-1362.27 = -787 - 857.4 - \Delta\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{f}\, [\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{OH}(\ell)]}^\circ$
$\Delta\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{f}\, [\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{OH}(\ell)]}^\circ = -2.82 \times 10^2\text{ KJ/mole}$
$\approx -3 \times 10^2$

subject: Chemistry
text: The total number of unpaired electrons present in the $d^3$, $d^4$ (low spin) $d^5$ (high spin), $d^6$ (high spin) and $d^7$ (low spin) octahedral complex systems is ______.
solution:
$d^3 \rightarrow \left[t_{2g}^3, e_g^0\right]$, 3 unpaired electrons

$d^5$ (high spin) $\rightarrow \left[t_{2g}^3, e_g^2\right]$, 5 unpaired electrons

text:
For the following gas phase equilibrium reaction at constant temperature,
$$\text{NH}_3(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons \frac{1}{2}\text{N}_2(\text{g}) + \frac{3}{2}\text{H}_2(\text{g})$$
If the total pressure is $\sqrt{3}$ atm and the pressure equilibrium constant ($K_p$) is $9$ atm, then the degree of dissociation is given as $(x \times 10^{-2})^{-1/2}$. The value of $x$ is ______ (Nearest integer)
solution:
$$\text{NH}_3(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons \frac{1}{2}\text{N}_2(\text{g}) + \frac{3}{2}\text{H}_2(\text{g})$$
$t=0 \quad 1 \text{ mole} \quad - \quad -$
$t=t_{eq} \quad 1-\alpha \quad \alpha/2 \quad 3\alpha/2$
$$K_p = \frac{\left(\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)^{1/2} \left(/frac{3\alpha}{2}\right)^{3/2}}{(1-\alpha)} \left[ \frac{P_T}{1+\alpha} \right]^1 \quad [\because P_T = \sqrt{3} \text{ atm}]$$
$$9 = \frac{\left(\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)^{1/2} \left(\frac{3\alpha}{2}\right)^{3/2}}{(1-\alpha)} \times \frac{(3)^{1/2}}{1+\alpha}$$
$$9 = \frac{9\left(\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)^2}{1-\alpha^2}$$
$$1 - \alpha^2 = \frac{\alpha^2}{4}$$
$$\frac{5\alpha^2}{4} = 1$$
$$\alpha^2 = 0.8$$
$$\alpha = (0.8)^{1/2}$$
$$\alpha = \left[ \frac{1}{0.8} \right]^{-1/2}$$
$$\alpha = \left[ 125 \times 10^{-2} \right]^{-1/2}$$
$x = 125$.

subject: Chemistry
text: Two liquids A and B form an ideal solution. At $320\text{ K}$, the vapour pressure of the solution, containing $3\text{ mol}$ of A and $1\text{ mol}$ of B is $500\text{ mm Hg}$. At the same temperature, if $1\text{ mol}$ of A is further added to this solution, vapour pressure of the solution increases by $20\text{ mm Hg}$. Vapour pressure (in $\text{mm Hg}$) of B in the pure state is ________. (Nearest integer)
solution:
$$X_A = \frac{3}{4}, X_B = \frac{1}{4}$$

$$P_S = P_A^o X_A + P_B^o X_B$$

$$500 = P_A^o \times \frac{3}{4} + P_B^o \times \frac{1}{4}$$

$$3P_A^o + P_B^o = 2000 \quad \text{..... (1)}$$

Now $1\text{ mole}$ of A is further added so $n_A = 4\text{ mole}$, $n_b = 1\text{ mole}$

$$X'_A = \frac{4}{5}, X'_B = \frac{1}{5}$$

$$P_S = 520 = P_A^o \times \frac{4}{5} + P_B^o \times \frac{1}{5}$$

$$4P_A^o + P_B^o = 2600 \quad \text{..... (2)}$$

By equation (2) $-$ equation (1)

$$P_A^o = 600\text{ mm Hg}$$

$$P_B^o = 200\text{ mm Hg}$$

text: The hydrogen spectrum consists of several spectral lines in Lyman series ($L_1, L_2, L_3 \dots$; $L_1$ has lowest energy among Lyman series). Similarly it consists of several spectral lines in Balmer series ($B_1, B_2, B_3 \dots \dots \dots$; $B_1$ has lowest energy among Balmer lines). The energy of $L_1$ is x times the energy of $B_1$. solution:
$$\Delta \text{E}(L_1) = 13.6 \times Z^2 \left(\frac{1}{1^2} - \frac{1}{2^2}\right) = 13.6 Z^2 \times \frac{3}{4}$$
$$\Delta \text{E}(B_1) = 13.6 \times Z^2 \times \left(\frac{1}{2^2} - \frac{1}{3^2}\right) = 13.6 \times Z^2 \times \frac{5}{4 \times 9}$$
$$\frac{\Delta \text{E}(L_1)}{\Delta \text{E}(B_1)} = \frac{3}{5} \times 9 = \frac{27}{5} = x$$
$$x = \left(\frac{27}{5} \times 10\right) \times 10^{-1} = 54 \times 10^{-1}$$

$$\Delta G^{\circ} = -6 \times 96500 \times 1.21\text{ J}$$

$$0.8 \times 6 \times 96500 \times 1.21 = 1 \times 10^3 (\Delta V)$$
$$\Delta V = 560.472\text{ m}^3$$

subject: Chemistry
text:
$2.0\text{ g}$ of a bromo hydrocarbon (X) was subjected to Carius analysis, gave $3.36\text{ g}$ of $\mathrm{AgBr}$. The percentage of carbon in the compound (X) is $26.7\%$. Total number of carbon atoms in the empirical formula for compound (X) is ______.
(Given molar mass in $\mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$ H : 1, C : 12, Br : 80, Ag : 108)
solution:
$n_{\mathrm{Br}} = \frac{3.36}{108+80}$
$r = \text{no. of Br atoms in organic compound}$
$n_{\mathrm{organic\ compound}} = \frac{3.36}{(108+80)\times r} = \frac{2}{M}$
$M = \frac{2\times 188 \times r}{3.36}$
$M = \frac{1}{2} \times x \text{ (x is integer)}$
$W_C = \frac{112 \times x \times 26.7}{100} = 30 \times x$
$n_C = \frac{30 \times x}{12} = 2.5 \times x$
Take $x = 2, n_C = 5$
(Empirical formula is $\mathrm{C_5H_4Br}$)

subject: Chemistry
text:
$20 \text{ g}$ hemoglobin in a $1 \text{ L}$ aqueous solution (A) at $300 \text{ K}$ is separated from pure water by semi permeable membrane. At equilibrium the height of solution in a tube dipped in a solution (A) is found to be $80.0 \text{ mm}$ higher than the tube dipped in water.
The molar mass of hemoglobin is ______ $\text{kg mol}^{-1}$. (Nearest integer)
(Given : $g = 10 \text{ ms}^{-2}$, $R = 8.3 \text{ kPa dm}^3\text{K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$, density of solution = $1000 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$)
solution:
Osmotic pressure, $\pi = \rho g h$
$= 1000 \times 10 \times 80 \times 10^{-3}$
$= 800 \text{ Pa} \quad \dots \dots (1)$

Let molar mass of haemoglobin = $\text{M g/mol}$
conc. of haemoglobin = $\frac{20/\text{M}}{10^{-3}} \left(\frac{\text{mol}}{\text{m}^3}\right)$

$\pi = \text{CRT} \text{ (S.I. units)}$
$\Rightarrow \pi = \left[\frac{20}{10^{-3}\text{M}}\right] \times 8.3 \times 300$
$= 800 \quad \text{[From (1)]}$

Solving we get :
$\text{M} = \frac{20 \times 8.3 \times 300}{0.8} \text{ g/mol}$
$= 62.25 \text{ kg mol}^{-1}$
Ans = $62$

subject: Chemistry
text: Identify the metal ions among $\text{Co}^{2+}$, $\text{Ni}^{2+}$, $\text{Fe}^{2+}$, $\text{V}^{3+}$ and $\text{Ti}^{2+}$ having a spin-only magnetic moment value more than $3.0\text{ BM}$. The sum of unpaired electrons present in the high spin octahedral complexes formed by those metal ions is $\underline{\quad\quad\quad\quad}$.
solution:
$\text{V}^{3+} = (\text{Ar})_{18} \text{ 3d}^2$
$\text{Ti}^{2+} = (\text{Ar})_{18} \text{ 3d}^2$
$\text{Ni}^{2+} = (\text{Ar})_{18} \text{ 3d}^8$
$\text{Fe}^{2+} = (\text{Ar})_{18} \text{ 3d}^6$
$\text{Co}^{2+} = (\text{Ar})_{18} \text{ 3d}^7$
Only for $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ and $\text{Co}^{2+}$ $\mu$ is more than $3.0\text{ B.M.}$
For $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ $3\text{d}^6$: unpaired electrons = $4$, $\mu > 3$
For $\text{Co}^{2+}$ $3\text{d}^7$: unpaired electrons = $3$, $\mu > 3$
$\therefore \text{Number of unpaired electrons} = 4 + 3 = 7$

subject: Chemistry
text:
Molar conductivity of a weak acid $\text{HQ}$ of concentration $0.18 \text{ M}$ was found to be $1/30$ of the molar conductivity of another weak acid $\text{HZ}$ with concentration of $0.02 \text{ M}$. If $\lambda_{\text{Q}^-}^0$ happened to be equal with $\lambda_{\text{Z}^-}^0$, then the difference of the $\text{pK}_\text{a}$ values of the two weak acids $(\text{pK}_\text{a}(\text{HQ}) - \text{pK}_\text{a}(\text{HZ}))$ is ______ . (Nearest integer)
[Given : degree of dissociation $(\alpha) \ll 1$ for both weak acids, $\lambda^0$ : limiting molar conductivity of ions]
solution:
$$K_a(\text{HQ}) = C_1\alpha_1^2, \quad \alpha_1 = \frac{\lambda_m(\text{HQ})}{\lambda_m^0(\text{HQ})}$$
$$K_a(\text{HZ}) = C_2\alpha_2^2, \quad \alpha_2 = \frac{\lambda_m(\text{HZ})}{\lambda_m^0(\text{HZ})}$$
$$\frac{K_a(\text{HQ})}{K_a(\text{HZ})} = \frac{C_1}{C_2} \left(\frac{\alpha_1}{\alpha_2}\right)^2 = \frac{0.18}{0.02} \left[\frac{\lambda_m(\text{HQ})}{\lambda_m(\text{HZ})}\right]^2$$
$$\frac{K_a(\text{HQ})}{K_a(\text{HZ})} = 9 \times \left(\frac{1}{30}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{100}$$
$$\text{pK}_\text{a}(\text{HQ}) - \text{pK}_\text{a}(\text{HZ}) = 2$$

subject: Chemistry
text:
For reaction $\text{A} \rightarrow \text{P}$, rate constant $k = 1.5 \times 10^3\text{ s}^{-1}$ at $27^{\circ}\text{C}$. If activation energy for the above reaction is $60\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, then the temperature (in $^{\circ}\text{C}$) at which rate constant, $k = 4.5 \times 10^3\text{ s}^{-1}$ is $\dots\dots$. (Nearest integer)
Given : $\log 2 = 0.30, \log 3 = 0.48, \text{R} = 8.3\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}, \ln 10 = 2.3$
solution:
$$\ln \left(\frac{K_2}{K_1}\right) = \frac{\text{E}_a}{\text{R}} \left[\frac{T_2 - T_1}{T_1 T_2}\right]$$

$$\ln \left(\frac{4.5 \times 10^3}{1.5 \times 10^3}\right) = \frac{60 \times 10^3}{8.3} \left[\frac{T_2 - 300}{300 T_2}\right]$$

$$\ln 3 = \frac{60 \times 10^3}{8.3} \left[\frac{T_2 - 300}{300 T_2}\right]$$

$$\Rightarrow T_2 = 314.4\text{ K}$$

$$\Rightarrow t = 41.4^{\circ}\text{C}$$, nearest integer is $41$

subject: Chemistry
text:
For a first order reaction $A \rightarrow B$

| $t / \text{min}$ | $[A] / \text{M}$ |
|---|---|
| $0$ | $0.6500$ |
| $x$ | $0.0650$ |
| $20$ | $0.00065$ |

$x = \text{______ } \text{min.}$ (Nearest integer)
solution:
$K = \frac{1}{t} \ln \left[\frac{A_0}{A_t}\right]$
$K = \frac{1}{20} \ln \left[\frac{0.6500}{0.00065}\right] \Rightarrow \frac{3\ln 10}{20} \text{ min}^{-1}$
Also, $x = \frac{1}{K} \ln \left[\frac{A_0}{A_x}\right] \Rightarrow \frac{20}{3\ln 10} \ln \left(\frac{0.6500}{0.0650}\right)$
$= \frac{20}{3} \text{min} \Rightarrow 6.7 \text{ min}$ (Nearest integer $7$)

\frac{1}{T}(\text{K}^{-1}) & \log_{10} \text{K}_p \\

subject: Chemistry
text:
In a closed flask at $600\text{ K}$, one mole of $\text{X}_2\text{Y}_4(\text{g})$ attains equilibrium as given below:
$$\text{X}_2\text{Y}_4(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{XY}_2(\text{g})$$
At equilibrium, $75\% \text{ X}_2\text{Y}_4(\text{g})$ was dissociated and the total pressure is $1\text{ atm}$. The magnitude of $\Delta_r \text{G}^\ominus$ (in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$) at this temperature is _______. (Nearest Integer)
(Given: $\text{R} = 8.3\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}$; $\ln 10 = 2.3$, $\log 2 = 0.3$, $\log 3 = 0.48$, $\log 5 = 0.69$, $\log 7 = 0.84$)
solution:
$$\text{X}_2\text{Y}_4(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{XY}_2(\text{g})$$
At $t=0$: $\text{P}^0$
At $t=t$: $\text{P}^0(1-\alpha)$ $2\text{P}^0\alpha$

$\text{P}^0(1+\alpha) = 1$
$\alpha = \frac{3}{4}$; $\text{P}^0 = \frac{4}{7}$

$\text{K}_p = \frac{4\text{P}_0\alpha^2}{1-\alpha^2} = \frac{36}{7}$

$\Delta\text{G}^\ominus = -\text{RT}\ln\text{k}_p$

$|\Delta\text{G}^\ominus| = 8.314 \times 600 \left|\ln\left(\frac{36}{7}\right)\right|$
$= 8169.5\text{ J mol}^{-1}$
$= 8.169\text{ kJ/mol}$

subject: Chemistry
text:
Consider the reaction :
$2\text{H}_2\text{S(g)} + 3\text{O}_2\text{g)} \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) + 2\text{SO}_2\text{g)}$
The magnitude of enthalpy change for the reaction in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ is ________. (Nearest integer)
Given : $\Delta_f \text{H}^{\ominus} (\text{H}_2\text{S}) = -20.1 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
$\Delta_f \text{H}^{\ominus} (\text{H}_2\text{O}) = -286.0 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
$\Delta_f \text{H}^{\ominus} (\text{SO}_2) = -297.0 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
solution:
$\Delta_r \text{H}^{\circ} = \Sigma \Delta_f \text{H}^{\circ}(\text{product}) - \Sigma \Delta_f \text{H}^{\circ}(\text{Reactant})$
$\Delta_r \text{H}^{\circ} = 2 \times \Delta_f \text{H}^{\circ}(\text{SO}_2, \text{g}) + 2 \times \Delta_f \text{H}^{\circ}(\text{H}_2\text{O}, \ell) - 2 \times \Delta_f \text{H}^{\circ}(\text{H}_2\text{S}, \text{g})$
$\Delta_r \text{H}^{\circ} = 2 \times (-297) + 2 \times (-286) - 2 \times (-20.1)$
$= -594 - 572 + 40.2$
$\Delta_r \text{H}^{\circ} = -1125.8 \text{ kJ/mol}$.
$|\Delta_r \text{H}^{\circ}| = 1125.8 \text{ kJ/mol}$.

subject: Chemistry
text:
Consider the following reactions:
$\text{NaCl} + \text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{A} + \text{KHSO}_4 + \text{NaHSO}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

text: The number of isoelectronic species among $\text{Sc}^{3+}$, $\text{Cr}^{2+}$, $\text{Mn}^{3+}$, $\text{Co}^{3+}$ and $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ is '$n$'. If '$n$' moles of $\text{AgCl}$ is formed during the reaction of complex with formula $\text{CoCl}_3(\text{en})_2\text{NH}_3$ with excess of $\text{AgNO}_3$ solution, then the number of electrons present in the $t_{2g}$ orbital of the complex is _________.
solution:
Counting the total number of electrons in each ion:
- $\text{Sc}^{3+} : 18$
- $\text{Cr}^{2+} : 22$
- $\text{Mn}^{3+} : 22$
- $\text{Co}^{3+} : 24$
- $\text{Fe}^{3+} : 23$

Here, $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ and $\text{Mn}^{3+}$ are isoelectronic (both have 22 electrons). Thus, $n = 2$.

Reacting the complex $\text{CoCl}_3(\text{en})_2\text{NH}_3$ with $n = 2$ moles of $\text{AgNO}_3$ means the complex formula is $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2\text{NH}_3\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2$ yielding 2 moles of $\text{AgCl}$ precipitate.

In this complex, $\text{Co}$ is in $+3$ oxidation state with $d^6$ configuration.
For a coordination number of 6 (octahedral complex), the electronic configuration in crystal field splitting is:
$t_{2g}^{2,2,2} \text{ e}_g^{0,0}$

Therefore, the number of electrons present in the $t_{2g}$ orbital is $2 + 2 + 2 = 6$.

subject: Chemistry
text:
The effect of temperature on spontaneity of reactions are represented as:
(A) $\Delta H = +$, $\Delta S = -$, Temperature: any T, Spontaneity: Non spontaneous
(B) $\Delta H = +$, $\Delta S = +$, Temperature: low T, Spontaneity: spontaneous
(C) $\Delta H = -$, $\Delta S = -$, Temperature: low T, Spontaneity: Non spontaneous
(D) $\Delta H = -$, $\Delta S = +$, Temperature: any T, Spontaneity: spontaneous
Which of the above are correct?
solution:
$\because \Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$
For spontaneity of reaction: $\Delta G = -\text{ve}$
(A) $\Delta H = +, \Delta S = - \implies \Delta G = + - T(-) = + + \text{ve} \implies$ Non-spontaneous at any T.
(B) $\Delta H = +, \Delta S = + \implies \Delta G = + - T(+) \implies$ Spontaneous at high T, Non-spontaneous at low T.
(C) $\Delta H = -, \Delta S = - \implies \Delta G = - - T(-) = - + \text{ve} \implies$ Spontaneous at high T, Non-spontaneous at low T.
(D) $\Delta H = -, \Delta S = + \implies \Delta G = - - T(+) \implies$ Spontaneous at any T.
Therefore, (B) and (C) are correct descriptions.

subject: Chemistry
text: For the given cell $\text{Fe}^{2+}(\text{aq}) + \text{Ag}^+(\text{aq}) \to \text{Fe}^{3+}(\text{aq}) + \text{Ag}(\text{s})$. The standard cell potential of the above reaction is given: $\text{Ag}^+ + e^- \to \text{Ag}, E^0 = x\text{ V}$; $\text{Fe}^{2+} + 2e^- \to \text{Fe}, E^0 = y\text{ V}$; $\text{Fe}^{3+} + 3e^- \to \text{Fe}, E^0 = z\text{ V}$.
solution:
Given reaction: $\text{Fe}^{2+}(\text{aq}) + \text{Ag}^+(\text{aq}) \to \text{Fe}^{3+}(\text{aq}) + \text{Ag}(\text{s})$
Using Gibbs free energy relations:
$\Delta G_3^0 = \Delta G_1^0 + \Delta G_2^0$
$-3F(-z) = -2F(-y) + \Delta G_2^0$
$\Delta G_2^0 = 3Fz - 2Fy$
Also $\Delta G_2^0 = -nFE_{\text{Fe}^{2+}/\text{Fe}^{3+}}^0$
$3Fz - 2Fy = -1F(E_{\text{Fe}^{2+}/\text{Fe}^{3+}}^0)$
$E_{\text{Fe}^{2+}/\text{Fe}^{3+}}^0 = 2y - 3z$
$E_{\text{Cell}}^0$ for reaction will be $E_{\text{Ag}^+/\text{Ag}}^0 + E_{\text{Fe}^{2+}/\text{Fe}^{3+}}^0 = x + 2y - 3z$

subject: Chemistry
text: The calculated spin-only magnetic moments of $\text{K}_3[\text{Fe}(\text{OH})_6]$ and $\text{K}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{OH})_6]$ respectively are :
solution:
In $\text{K}_3[\text{Fe}(\text{OH})_6]$, Iron is in $+3$ oxidation state ($\text{Fe}^{3+}$), which has $d^5$ configuration. $\text{OH}^-$ is a weak field ligand, so number of unpaired electrons $n = 5$. Spin-only magnetic moment $\mu = \sqrt{5(5+2)} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.92$ B.M.
In $\text{K}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{OH})_6]$, Iron is in $+2$ oxidation state ($\text{Fe}^{2+}$), which has $d^6$ configuration. $\text{OH}^-$ is a weak field ligand, so number of unpaired electrons $n = 4$. Spin-only magnetic moment $\mu = \sqrt{4(4+2)} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.90$ B.M.

(1) The concentration of $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ in the original mixture is $0.005\text{ M}$
(2) The concentration of $\text{HCl}$ in the original mixture is $0.005\text{ M}$
(3) $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ is neutralised first followed by neutralisation of $\text{HCl}$
(4) Point 'C' indicates the complete neutralisation $\text{HCl}$

options.1: The concentration of $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ in the original mixture is $0.005\text{ M}$
options.2: The concentration of $\text{HCl}$ in the original mixture is $0.005\text{ M}$
options.3: $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ is neutralised first followed by neutralisation of $\text{HCl}$

solution:
From the given graph $2\text{ mL}$ $\text{NaOH}$ solution is used for neutralisation of $\text{HCl}$ and $3\text{ mL}$ $\text{NaOH}$ solution is used for neutralisation of $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$.
$\therefore \text{Mole of } \text{HCl} = \text{Mole of } \text{NaOH used}$
$M \times 40 = 0.1 \times 2$
$M = 0.005$
$\therefore \text{Mole of } \text{CH}_3\text{COOH} = \text{Mole of } \text{NaOH used}$
$M \times 40 = 0.1 \times 3$
$M = 0.0075$
$\text{HCl}$ is strong acid and will be neutralised first.

subject: Chemistry
text:
$XY$ is the membrane / partition between two chambers 1 and 2 containing sugar solutions of concentration $c_1$ and $c_2$ ($c_1 > c_2$) $\text{mol L}^{-1}$. For the reverse osmosis to take place identify the correct condition
(Here $p_1$ and $p_2$ are pressures applied on chamber 1 and 2)

(A) Membrane/Partition ; Cellophane, $p_1 > \pi$
(B) Membrane/Partition ; Porous, $p_2 > \pi$
(C) Membrane/Partition ; Parchment paper, $p_1 > \pi$
(D) Membrane/Partition ; Cellophane, $p_2 > \pi$

Choose the correct answer from the option given below :
solution:
Normal osmosis occurs from (2) to (1).
For reverse osmosis from (1) to (2), pressure applied on chamber 1 must be greater than osmotic pressure, i.e., $P_1 > \pi$, using semipermeable membrane like Cellophane or Parchment paper.
Therefore, (A) and (C) are correct.

text:
The correct order of basicity for the following molecules is :

(P) 
(Q) 
(R)
solution: According to Bredt's rule, the lone pair on nitrogen in molecule (R) is localized because it cannot participate in bridgehead double bond resonance. In (Q), there is cross conjugation, and in (P) the lone pair is delocalized into the carbonyl group. Thus, the basicity order is $R > Q > P$.

text:
Heat treatment of muscular pain involves radiation of wavelength of about $900 \text{ nm}$. Which spectral line of H atom is suitable for this?
Given: Rydberg constant $R_H = 10^5 \text{ cm}^{-1}, h = 6.6 \times 10^{-34} \text{ J s}, c = 3 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$
solution:
$\lambda = 900 \text{ nm} \quad \text{H-atom } (Z = 1)$
$= 9 \times 10^{-5} \text{ cm}$
$R_H = 10^5 \text{ cm}^{-1}$

Rydberg eq. = $\frac{1}{\lambda} = R_H Z^2 \times \left(\frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2}\right)$

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{\lambda \times R_H} = \frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{9 \times 10^{-5} \text{ cm} \times 10^5 \text{ cm}^{-1}} = \left(\frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2}\right)$

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2} = \frac{1}{9}$

It is possible when $n_1 = 3, n_2 = \infty$
Possible series : $\infty \to 3$

text:
Given below are two statements :
**Statement I :** In the oxalic acid vs $\text{KMnO}_4$ (in the presence of dil $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$) titration the solution needs to be heated initially to $60^\circ\text{C}$, but no heating is required in Ferrous ammonium sulphate (FAS) vs $\text{KMnO}_4$ titration (in the presence of dil $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$).
**Statement II :** In oxalic acid vs $\text{KMnO}_4$ titration, the initial formation of $\text{MnSO}_4$ takes place at high temperature, which then acts as catalyst for further reaction. In the case of FAS vs $\text{KMnO}_4$, heating oxidizes $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ into $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ by oxygen of air and error may be introduced in the experiment.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.1: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
options.2: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.3: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options.4: Both Statement I and Statement II are false

solution:
For the titration : Oxalic acid v/s $\text{KMnO}_4$
$$2\text{MnO}_4^- + 5(\text{COO})_2^{2-} + 16\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 10\text{CO}_2 + 2\text{Mn}^{2+} + 8\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
This reaction is slow at room temperature, but becomes fast at $60^\circ\text{C}$. Manganese(II) ions catalyse the reaction; thus, the reaction is autocatalytic; once manganese(II) ions are formed, it becomes faster and faster.
The titration of FAS v/s $\text{KMnO}_4$ do not require heating because at higher temperature the oxidation of $\text{Fe}^{+2}$ to $\text{Fe}^{+3}$ by atmospheric $\text{O}_2$ will be prominent.

subject: Chemistry
text:
For hydrogen like species, which of the following graphs provides the most appropriate representation of E vs Z plot for a constant n ?
[E : Energy of the stationary state,
Z : atomic number, n = principal quantum number]
solution:
The energy of the stationary state for hydrogen-like species is given by:
$$E = -13.6 \times \frac{Z^2}{n^2} \text{ eV}$$
For a constant $n$, $E$ is directly proportional to $-Z^2$. Thus, $E$ vs $Z$ represents a parabola opening downwards, passing through the origin, with negative energy values.

text:
Let us consider a reversible reaction at temperature, $T$.
In this reaction, both $\Delta H$ and $\Delta S$ were observed to have positive values. If the equilibrium temperature is $T_e$, then the reaction becomes spontaneous at :
solution:
For reaction to be spontaneous according to $2^\text{nd}$ law:
$\Delta G < 0$
$\Rightarrow \Delta H - T\Delta S < 0$
$\Rightarrow T > \left(\frac{\Delta H}{\Delta S}\right) = T_e$
$\Rightarrow T > T_e$

The property/properties that show irregularity in first four elements of group-17 is/are :
(A) Covalent radius
(B) Electron affinity
(C) Ionic radius
(D) First ionization energy
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
solution:
The order of first four elements of group-17 are as follows:
- $\mathrm{F < Cl < Br < I}$ (Covalent radius)
- $\mathrm{Cl > F > Br > I}$ (Electron affinity)
- $\mathrm{F^- < Cl^- < Br^- < I^-}$ (Ionic radius)
- $\mathrm{F > Cl > Br > I}$ ($1^{\text{st}}$ ionization energy)

Electron affinity order is irregular.

text:
Given below are two statements :

**Statement I :** $\text{Et}_2\text{N}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl}$ will undergo alkaline hydrolysis at a faster rate than $\text{Et}_2\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl}$.

**Statement II :** $\text{Et}_2\text{N}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl}$, intramolecular substitution takes place first by involving lone pair of electrons on nitrogen.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

options.1: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.2: Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
options.3: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.4: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

solution: The compound $\text{Et}_2\text{N}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl}$ undergoes intramolecular nucleophilic substitution where the nitrogen lone pair attacks the adjacent carbon to form an aziridinium ion intermediate, which then undergoes ring opening by $\text{OH}^-$ attack. Thus, both statements are correct.

subject: Chemistry
text: At temperature T, compound $\text{AB}_{2(\text{g})}$ dissociates as $\text{AB}_{2(\text{g})} \rightleftharpoons \text{AB}_{(\text{g})} + \frac{1}{2}\text{B}_{2(\text{g})}$ having degree of dissociation x (small compared to unity). The correct expression for x in terms of $\text{K}_{\text{p}}$ and p is
solution:
$$\text{AB}_{2(\text{g})} \rightleftharpoons \text{AB}_{(\text{g})} + \frac{1}{2}\text{B}_{2(\text{g})}$$
At $t_{\text{eq.}}$:
$\text{AB}_2: \frac{(1-x)}{1+\frac{x}{2}}\text{p}$
$\text{AB}: \frac{x\text{p}}{1+\frac{x}{2}}$
$\text{B}_2: \frac{(\frac{x}{2})\text{p}}{1+\frac{x}{2}}$
$\Rightarrow x \ll 1 \Rightarrow 1 + \frac{x}{2} \simeq 1$ and $1 - x \simeq 1$
$\Rightarrow \text{K}_{\text{p}} = \frac{(\text{x}\text{p}).(\frac{\text{xp}}{2})^{\frac{1}{2}}}{\text{p}}$
$\Rightarrow \text{K}_{\text{p}}^2 = \text{x}^2 \cdot \frac{\text{xp}}{2}$
$\Rightarrow \text{x} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{2\text{K}_{\text{p}}^2}{\text{p}}}$

text:
Total enthalpy change for freezing of $1\text{ mol}$ of water at $10^\circ\text{C}$ to ice at $-10^\circ\text{C}$ is ______

(Given : $\Delta_{\text{fus}}\text{H} = x\text{ kJ/mol}$
$C_p[\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})] = y\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}$
$C_p[\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{s})] = z\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}$)
solution:
Path for phase change:
$$\begin{matrix} \text{H}_2\text{O}_{(l)} 10^\circ\text{C} & \xrightarrow{} & \text{H}_2\text{O}_{(s)} 10^\circ\text{C} \\ nC_{p(l)}\Delta T \Big\downarrow & & \Big\uparrow nC_{p(s)}\Delta T \\ \text{H}_2\text{O}_{(l)} 0^\circ\text{C} & \xrightarrow[-\Delta_{\text{fusion}}H]{} & \text{H}_2\text{O}_{(s)} 0^\circ\text{C} \end{matrix}$$

$$\Delta \text{H} = 1 \times y(0 - 10) - x \times 1000 + 1 \times z(-10^\circ - 0^\circ)$$
$$\Delta \text{H} = -10(100x + y + z)\text{ Joule.}$

subject: Chemistry
text: Consider the reaction $\text{X}_2\text{Y(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{X}_2\text{(g)} + \frac{1}{2}\text{Y}_2\text{(g)}$. The equation representing correct relationship between the degree of dissociation (x) of $\text{X}_2\text{Y(g)}$ with its equilibrium constant Kp is _______. Assume x to be very very small.
solution:
1 mole of $\text{X}_2\text{Y(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{X}_2\text{(g)} + \frac{1}{2}\text{Y}_2\text{(g)}$
At equilibrium: $(1-x)$ mole, $x$ mole, $\frac{x}{2}$ mole
Total moles = $1 - x + x + \frac{x}{2} = 1 + \frac{x}{2}$
$P_{X_2Y} = \frac{1-x}{1+\frac{x}{2}} \times P$
$P_{X_2} = \frac{x}{1+\frac{x}{2}} \times P$
$P_{Y_2} = \frac{x/2}{1+\frac{x}{2}} \times P$
$K_p = \frac{P_{X_2} \cdot (P_{Y_2})^{1/2}}{P_{X_2Y}} = \frac{\left(\frac{x}{1+\frac{x}{2}}\times P\right)\left(\frac{x/2}{1+\frac{x}{2}}\times P\right)^{1/2}}{\left(\frac{1-x}{1+\frac{x}{2}}\times P\right)}$
Since $x$ is very very small, $1-x \approx 1$ and $1+\frac{x}{2} \approx 1$.
$K_p \approx \frac{x \cdot \left(\frac{x}{2}\right)^{1/2} \cdot P^{1/2}}{1} = \frac{x^{3/2}}{2^{1/2}} \cdot P^{1/2}$
$x^{3/2} = \frac{K_p \cdot 2^{1/2}}{P^{1/2}}$
Squaring both sides:
$x^3 = \frac{K_p^2 \cdot 2}{P}$
$x = \left(\frac{K_p^2 \times 2}{P}\right)^{1/3}$

subject: Chemistry
text: A weak acid $\text{HA}$ has degree of dissociation $x$. Which option gives the correct expression of $\text{pH} = \text{pK}_\text{a}$?
solution:
For dissociation of weak acid $\text{HA} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+ + \text{A}^-$
At $t=0$: $a$, $0$, $0$
At equilibrium: $a(1-x)$, $ax$, $ax$
$K_a = \frac{(ax)(ax)}{a(1-x)} = \frac{a x^2}{1-x}$, and $[\text{H}^+] = ax$
$-\log(K_a) = -\log(ax) - \log\left(\frac{x}{1-x}\right)$
$\text{pK}_a = \text{pH} - \log\left(\frac{x}{1-x}\right)$
For $\text{pH} = \text{pK}_a$, we must have $\log\left(\frac{x}{1-x}\right) = 0$, wait, let's look at the options or standard form:

text: In a reaction $A + B \rightarrow C$, initial concentrations of A and B are related as $[A]_0 = 8[B]_0$. The half lives of A and B are $10\text{ min}$ and $40\text{ min}$ respectively. If they start to disappear at the same time, both following first order kinetics, after how much time will the concentration of both the reactants be same?
solution: Given: $[A]_0 = 8[B]_0$, $[t_{1/2}]_A = 10\text{ min}$, $[t_{1/2}]_B = 40\text{ min}$. First order kinetics. Let at time $t$, $[A]_t = [B]_t$. Since $-k_A \times t$ and $-k_B \times t$, we have $[A]_0 e^{-k_A t} = [B]_0 e^{-k_B t} \implies \frac{[A]_0}{[B]_0} = e^{(k_A - k_B)t} \implies 8 = e^{(k_A - k_B)t} \implies \ln 8 = (k_A - k_B)t \implies \ln 8 = \ln 2 \left(\frac{1}{(t_{1/2})_A} - \frac{1}{(t_{1/2})_B}\right) \times t$. Solving gives $t = 40\text{ min}$.

text:
Consider the equilibrium
$\text{CO(g)} + 3\text{H}_2\text{g} \rightleftharpoons \text{CH}_4\text{g} + \text{H}_2\text{O(g)}$
If the pressure applied over the system increases by two fold at constant temperature then
(A) Concentration of reactants and products increases.
(B) Equilibrium will shift in forward direction.
(C) Equilibrium constant increases since concentration of products increases.
(D) Equilibrium constant remains unchanged as concentration of reactants and products remain same.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
(1) (A) and (B) only
(2) (A), (B) and (D) only
(3) (B) and (C) only
(4) (A), (B) and (C) only
solution: When pressure is increased by twofold at constant temperature, the volume decreases, leading to an increase in concentration of both reactants and products (Statement A). According to Le Chatelier's principle, the equilibrium shifts in the direction of fewer moles of gas (forward direction here, since $\Delta n_g = 2 - 4 = -2$) (Statement B). Equilibrium constant $K$ only depends on temperature, hence it remains unchanged.

A. The order of the reaction is $\frac{1}{2}$.
B. If $[\text{A}]_0$ is $1\text{ M}$, then $t_{1/2}$ is $200\sqrt{10}\text{ min}$.
C. The order of the reaction changes to $1$ if the concentration of reactant changes from $0.100\text{ M}$ to $0.500\text{ M}$.
D. $t_{1/2}$ is $800\text{ min}$ for $[\text{A}]_0 = 1.6\text{ M}$.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution:
Let order be $n$. $t_{1/2} \propto [\text{A}]_0^{1-n}$.
$\frac{t_{1/2}(1)}{t_{1/2}(2)} = \left(\frac{[	ext{A}]_{0,1}}{[\text{A}]_{0,2}}\right)^{1-n} \Rightarrow \frac{200}{100} = \left(\frac{0.100}{0.025}\right)^{1-n} \Rightarrow 2 = (4)^{1-n} \Rightarrow 2^1 = 2^{2(1-n)} \Rightarrow 1 = 2 - 2n \Rightarrow n = 1/2$.
Thus Statement A is true.
For $n = 1/2$, $t_{1/2} = k \cdot [\text{A}]_0^{1-1/2} = k \sqrt{[\text{A}]_0}$.
At $[\text{A}]_0 = 0.1$, $t_{1/2} = 200 \Rightarrow 200 = k \sqrt{0.1} \Rightarrow k = \frac{200}{\sqrt{0.1}} = 200\sqrt{10}$.
If $[\text{A}]_0 = 1$, $t_{1/2} = 200\sqrt{10} \times \sqrt{1} = 200\sqrt{10}\text{ min}$. Statement B is true.
For $[\text{A}]_0 = 1.6\text{ M}$, $t_{1/2} = 200\sqrt{10} \times \sqrt{1.6} = 200\sqrt{16} = 200 \times 4 = 800\text{ min}$. Statement D is true.
Therefore, A, B, and D are correct.

text: For $A_2 + B_2 \rightleftharpoons 2AB$, $E_a$ for forward and backward reaction are 180 and $200 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ respectively. If catalyst lowers $E_a$ for both reaction by $100 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. Which of the following statement is correct?

options.1: Catalyst does not alter the Gibbs energy change of a reaction.
options.2: Catalyst can cause non-spontaneous reactions to occur.
options.3: The enthalpy change for the reaction is $+20 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.
options.4: The enthalpy change for the catalysed reaction is different from that of uncatalysed reaction.

solution:
$A_2 + B_2 \rightleftharpoons 2AB$
$E_f = 180 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
$E_b = 200 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
$\Delta H = E_f - E_b = -20 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
In presence of catalyst :
$E_f = 180 - 100 = 80 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
$E_b = 200 - 100 = 100 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
Catalyst does not change $\Delta H$ or $\Delta G$ of a reaction.

text:
Given below are two statements :

**Statement (I) :** Molal depression constant $K_f$ is given by $\frac{M_1 R T_f}{\Delta S_{\text{fus}}}$, where symbols have their usual meaning.

**Statement (II) :** $K_f$ for benzene is less than the $K_f$ for water.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

options.1: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.2: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.3: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.4: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

solution:
Statement-I:
Molar depression constant $k_f = \frac{M_1 R T_f^2}{\Delta H_{\text{fus}}}$
$k_f = \frac{M_1 R T_f}{\left[\frac{\Delta H_{\text{fus}}}{T_f}\right]}$
$k_f = \frac{M_1 R T_f}{\Delta S_{\text{fus}}}$
Hence statement-I is correct.

But $k_f$ for benzene = $5.12 \; \frac{\text{°C}}{\text{molal}}$
$k_f$ for water = $1.86 \; \frac{\text{°C}}{\text{molal}}$
Hence statement-II is incorrect.

(A) $\mathrm{dG} = \mathrm{VdP} - \mathrm{SdI}$. At constant pressure, $\mathrm{dG} = -\mathrm{SdT} \implies \left(\frac{\partial G}{\partial T}\right)_P = -\mathrm{S}$ (Matches II)

text: Ice at $-5^{\circ}\text{C}$ is heated to become vapor with temperature of $110^{\circ}\text{C}$ at atmospheric pressure. The entropy change associated with this process can be obtained from :
solution:
The process can be divided into 5 steps:
1. Ice (268 K) $ightarrow$ Ice (273 K)
2. Ice (273 K) $ightarrow$ Water (273 K)
3. Water (273 K) $ightarrow$ Water (373 K)
4. Water (373 K) $ightarrow$ Water vapour (373 K)
5. Water vapour (373 K) $ightarrow$ Water vapour (383 K)

Total entropy change $\Delta	ext{S}_{	ext{overall}} = \Delta	ext{S}_1 + \Delta	ext{S}_2 + \Delta	ext{S}_3 + \Delta	ext{S}_4 + \Delta	ext{S}_5$
- $\Delta	ext{S}_1 = \int_{268	ext{K}}^{273	ext{K}}  rac{	ext{C}_{	ext{p,m}}	ext{dT}}{	ext{T}}$
- $\Delta	ext{S}_2 =  rac{\Delta	ext{H}_{	ext{m fusion}}}{273} =  rac{\Delta	ext{H}_{	ext{m fusion}}}{	ext{T}_{	ext{f}}}$ where $	ext{T}_{	ext{f}} = 273 	ext{ K}$
- $\Delta	ext{S}_3 = \int_{273	ext{K}}^{373	ext{K}}  rac{	ext{C}_{	ext{p,m}}	ext{dT}}{	ext{T}}$
- $\Delta	ext{S}_4 =  rac{\Delta	ext{H}_{	ext{m vaporisation}}}{373} =  rac{\Delta	ext{H}_{	ext{m vaporisation}}}{	ext{T}_{	ext{b}}}$ where $	ext{T}_{	ext{b}} = 373 	ext{ K}$
- $\Delta	ext{S}_5 = \int_{373	ext{K}}^{383	ext{K}}  rac{	ext{C}_{	ext{p,m}}	ext{dT}}{	ext{T}}$

Summing all these gives option (2).

subject: Chemistry
text: Ice and water are placed in a closed container at a pressure of $1\text{ atm}$ and temperature $273.15\text{ K}$. If pressure of the system is increased $2$ times, keeping temperature constant, then identify correct observation from following :
solution: From Le Chatelier's principle and the phase diagram of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, ice has a higher volume than water, so increasing pressure shifts equilibrium towards the liquid phase (denser phase). At $2\text{ atm}$, the freezing point decreases, and ice converts entirely to liquid water. Thus, the solid phase (ice) disappears completely.

text:
The standard cell potential ($E^{\theta}_{\text{cell}}$) of a fuel cell based on the oxidation of methanol in air that has been used to power television relay station is measured as $1.21\text{ V}$. The standard half cell reduction potential for $\text{O}_2$ ($E^{\theta}_{\text{O}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O}}$) is $1.229\text{ V}$.

Choose the correct statement:
(1) The standard half cell reduction potential for the reduction of $\text{CO}_2$ ($E^{\theta}_{\text{CO}_2/\text{CH}_3\text{OH}}$) is $19\text{ mV}$
(2) Oxygen is formed at the anode.
(3) Reactants are fed at one go to each electrode.
(4) Reduction of methanol takes place at the cathode.

options.1: The standard half cell reduction potential for the reduction of $\text{CO}_2$ ($E^{\theta}_{\text{CO}_2/\text{CH}_3\text{OH}}$) is $19\text{ mV}$
options.2: Oxygen is formed at the anode.
options.3: Reactants are fed at one go to each electrode.
options.4: Reduction of methanol takes place at the cathode.

solution:
$$\begin{aligned} E^{\theta}_{\text{cell}} &= E^{\theta}_{\text{cathode}} - E^{\theta}_{\text{Anode}} \\[6pt] 1.21 &= 1.229 - E^{\theta}_{\text{Anode}} \end{aligned}$$
Fuel cell involves oxidation of methanol which will occur at anode and reduction of $\text{O}_2$ will occur at cathode.

subject: Chemistry
text:
At the sea level, the dry air mass percentage composition is given as nitrogen gas : 70.0, oxygen gas : 27.0 and argon gas : 3.0. If total pressure is 1.15 atm, then calculate the ratio of followings respectively :
(i) partial pressure of nitrogen gas to partial pressure of oxygen gas
(ii) partial pressure of oxygen gas to partial pressure of argon gas
(Given : Molar mass of N, O and Ar are 14, 16, and 40 g mol$^{-1}$ respectively)
solution:
$\frac{P_{\text{N}_2}}{P_{\text{O}_2}} = \frac{x_{\text{N}_2} \cdot P_{\text{T}}}{x_{\text{O}_2} \cdot P_{\text{T}}} = \frac{n_{\text{N}_2}}{n_{\text{O}_2}}$ {using Dalton's law of partial pressure}
$= \frac{70/28}{27/32} = 2.96$
$\frac{P_{\text{O}_2}}{P_{\text{Ar}}} = \frac{n_{\text{O}_2}}{n_{\text{Ar}}} = \frac{27/32}{3/40} = 11.25$

subject: Chemistry
text: Liquid A and B form an ideal solution. The vapour pressure of pure liquids A and B are $350$ and $750$ $\text{mm Hg}$ respectively at the same temperature. If $x_{\text{A}}$ and $x_{\text{B}}$ are the mole fraction of A and B in solution while $y_{\text{A}}$ and $y_{\text{B}}$ are the mole fraction of A and B in vapour phase then :
solution:
$P^\circ_{\text{A}} < P^\circ_{\text{B}}$
$$\frac{P^\circ_{\text{A}}}{P^\circ_{\text{B}}} < 1$$
$$\frac{y_{\text{A}}}{y_{\text{B}}} = \frac{P^\circ_{\text{A}} x_{\text{A}}}{P^\circ_{\text{B}} x_{\text{B}}}$$
$$\frac{\frac{y_{\text{A}}}{y_{\text{B}}}}{\frac{x_{\text{A}}}{x_{\text{B}}}} < 1$$
$$\frac{y_{\text{A}}}{y_{\text{B}}} < \frac{x_{\text{A}}}{x_{\text{B}}}$$
Therefore, $\frac{x_{\text{A}}}{x_{\text{B}}} > \frac{y_{\text{A}}}{y_{\text{B}}}$

text:
$\text{HA(aq)} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+\text{(aq)} + \text{A}^-\text{(aq)}$
The freezing point depression of a $0.1 \text{ m}$ aqueous solution of a monobasic weak acid $\text{HA}$ is $0.20^\circ\text{C}$.
The dissociation constant for the acid is
Given :
$\text{K}_f(\text{H}_2\text{O}) = 1.8 \text{ K kg mol}^{-1}$, $\text{molality} = \text{molarity}$
solution:
$\Delta \text{T}_f = i \text{K}_f \text{m}$
$0.2 = i \times 1.8 \times 0.1$
$i = \frac{20}{18} = \frac{10}{9}$

For $\text{HA(aq)} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+\text{(aq)} + \text{A}^-\text{(aq)}$
$t = 0 \quad 1$
$t = t_{\text{eq}} \quad 1 - \alpha \quad \alpha \quad \alpha$
$i = 1 + \alpha$
$\frac{10}{9} = 1 + \alpha$
$\alpha = \frac{1}{9}$

$\text{K}_{\text{eq}} = \frac{[\text{H}^+][\text{A}^-]}{[\text{HA}]} = \frac{\text{C}\alpha^2}{1 - \alpha}$

$\text{K}_{\text{eq}} = 1.38 \times 10^{-3}$

subject: Chemistry
text: The correct order of the following complexes in terms of their crystal field stabilization energies is :
solution:
Order of CFSE depends on metal ion oxidation state (charge) and ligand strength.
$\text{Charge } \uparrow \implies \text{CFSE } \uparrow$
$\text{On increasing strength of ligand } \mathrm{CFSE} \uparrow$
SFL: $\mathrm{NH_3} < \mathrm{en}$
Comparison:
1. $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_4}]^{2+}$ ($Co^{2+}$, tetrahedral or lower coordination)
2. $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_6}]^{2+}$ ($Co^{2+}$, octahedral, lower charge)
3. $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_6}]^{3+}$ ($Co^{3+}$, octahedral, higher charge)
4. $[\mathrm{Co(en)_3}]^{3+}$ ($Co^{3+}$, octahedral, stronger ligand 'en' than $\mathrm{NH_3}$)
Thus, the correct order is:
$[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_4}]^{2+} < [\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_6}]^{2+} < [\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_6}]^{3+} < [\mathrm{Co(en)_3}]^{3+}$
